page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose ARM64 instance based on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 hardware running at 3.3 GHz and driven by the Nitro System hypervisor. The hardware layout supplies 48 physical cores mapped directly to 48 dedicated vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading. Cache resources include 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core alongside a shared 48 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 192 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The host includes 2850 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and 25 Gbps of baseline networking capacity without integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results show top-tier execution in multi-threaded decompression, software compilation with Clang, and static web serving throughput measuring 104.04 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations place in the top percentiles, complemented by top-tier in-memory Redis processing at 136.39 million operations per second and strong PassMark multi-core metrics. While prompt processing for small language models performs at a top-tier rate, sustained text generation throughput on small models drops to lower percentiles, marking a workload limitation for generative sequence synthesis.

The presence of 2850 GB directly attached NVMe storage paired with 48 non-oversubscribed cores makes this instance resource-dense for heavy I/O operations without incurring network storage latency. The balance of high single-thread clock rates, high memory bandwidth, and integrated disk capacity suits relational database hosting, distributed caching layers, software compilation clusters, data transformation, and concurrent web delivery.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose, ARM64 cloud instance built on AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 processors running at 3.3 GHz and managed via the Nitro hypervisor. The hardware profile features 48 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with single-threading, 192 GB of RAM offering 4.0 GB per core, and 2850 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage. It provides a baseline network throughput of 25 Gbps without GPU hardware. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across software compilation, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, static web serving throughput of 104.04 GB/sec, and in-memory Redis operations exceeding 136 million operations per second. However, generative LLM token production displays lower throughput efficiency. With dedicated physical cores, high local storage capacity, and balanced memory, the instance is configured for distributed databases, caching clusters, web architectures, CI/CD compilation workloads, and intensive data processing tasks.
